findings.title: self-heal-pipeline.md failure-mode table still says Bump 'version' in closed.json after field was renamed to 'schema_version'
findings.detail: Line 305 of docs/self-heal-pipeline.md in the 'Fingerprint drifted' failure-mode row advises: 'Bump `version` in `closed.json`'. However, the `version` field was renamed to `schema_version` in the 2026-05-24 nightly audit (AUDIT-ae-d9e0f1a2), and line 65 of the same file documents this rename. The failure-mode table row was not updated when the rename was made, creating an internal contradiction within the same document. This is a regression — the prior fix (AUDIT-audit-elevation-9f3c1d2e) updated the field-rules prose in §Field rules but missed the failure-mode table.
findings.fix_sketch: Change 'Bump `version` in `closed.json`' to 'Bump `schema_version` in `closed.json`' in the Fingerprint drifted recovery column on line 305.

findings.title: ADR-003 context paragraph describes finding lifecycle as 'closed/reopened' but the system uses 'closed' and 'regression' — 'reopened' is not a valid status
findings.detail: Line 123 of docs/ifleet-integration-adrs.md describes the audit finding lifecycle as 'opened → fixing → verifying → closed/reopened'. The actual canonical lifecycle defined in plan.md and rubric.json uses 'open → fixing → verifying → fixed → closed | regression'. The status 'reopened' was never defined in the rubric, the schema, or any scanner — 're-opened' findings appear as new findings with status 'regression'. A prior fix (AUDIT-audit-elevation-b2d5a9e3) updated the trace event payload to drop the reopened field but left this context paragraph unchanged, making ADR-003's lifecycle description inconsistent with the surrounding spec.
findings.fix_sketch: Change 'closed/reopened' on line 123 to 'closed | regression' to match the actual status lifecycle documented in plan.md and rubric.json.

findings.title: README.md reports 7 open decisions in Proposer spec but proposer-spec.md says eight (D1-D7 plus ADR-001)
findings.detail: README.md Open decisions section states 'Plus 7 open decisions in the Proposer spec (D1-D7)'. However, proposer-spec.md's plain-language recap section (last line) explicitly says 'The eight open decisions at the bottom (D1–D7 plus ADR-001)'. The proposer-spec contains 7 numbered decisions (D1–D7) plus one embedded ADR (ADR-Proposer-001), totalling 8 decision points Sebastian must answer. The README undercounts by 1.
findings.fix_sketch: Change '7 open decisions in the Proposer spec (D1-D7)' to '8 open decisions in the Proposer spec (D1-D7 plus ADR-Proposer-001)' in the Open decisions section of README.md.

findings.title: README.md 'Where the code lives' table lists rubric.json with its internal machine path instead of its repo-relative path
findings.detail: README.md line 217, in the 'Where the code lives' table under '**Config**', shows rubric.json path as `~/dev/ai-products/audit-elevation/rubric.json`. This is the absolute machine path on Sebastian's Mac, not a usable reference for anyone reading the repo. Since rubric.json lives at the root of this repo, the path should be `./rubric.json` or just `rubric.json` — consistent with how plan.md, docs/, and other files are referenced in the same table.
findings.fix_sketch: Change the rubric.json path from '~/dev/ai-products/audit-elevation/rubric.json' to 'rubric.json' in the Where the code lives table (line 217).
